definitions.explanation: The time when darkness gives way to light; the first light of morning. A formal/literary word for dawn.

examples.japanese: {払暁|ふつぎょう}に{出発|しゅっぱつ}した。
{部隊|ぶたい}は{払暁|ふつぎょう}に{攻撃|こうげき}を{開始|かいし}した。
examples.english: The troops launched an attack at dawn.

examples.japanese: {払暁|ふつぎょう}の{空|そら}に{一番星|いちばんぼし}がまだ{光|ひか}っていた。
examples.english: The morning star was still shining in the dawn sky.

notes:
FORMALITY: Formal/literary. Often used in historical or military contexts. In everyday speech, {明|あ}け{方|がた}, {夜明|よあ}け, or {早朝|そうちょう} are more common.

ETYMOLOGY: {払|ふつ} (to sweep away) + {暁|ぎょう} (dawn) - suggests the sweeping away of darkness.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {払暁|ふつぎょう}に{出発|しゅっぱつ}する (to depart at dawn)
- {払暁|ふつぎょう}の{攻撃|こうげき} (dawn attack)
- {払暁|ふつぎょう}の{空|そら} (the dawn sky)

RELATED WORDS:
- {夜明|よあ}け (daybreak - more common)
- {明|あ}け{方|がた} (dawn - everyday word)
- {暁|あかつき} (dawn - literary, also means "when/if")
- {黎明|れいめい} (dawn - literary, also figurative)
